problem_statement: ZMS (Zephyr Memory Storage) needs an API to report how many times its storage sectors have been recycled, so write-cycle consumption can be estimated. A caller must be able to query the maximum recycle count across all sectors and the recycle count of any individual sector. These queries must reject a NULL file-system pointer or NULL output pointer (-EINVAL), must reject an out-of-range sector index (-EINVAL), and must reject an unmounted file system (-EACCES). The returned count must grow correctly as sectors are recycled (e.g. after N sector advances it increases by the number of full recycle cycles), and the count must be preserved across zms_clear() and re-mounting rather than being reset to zero, even past the historical 8-bit counter wraparound at 256.

problem_statement_fixed: ZMS (Zephyr Memory Storage) needs an API to report how many times its storage sectors have been recycled, so write-cycle consumption can be estimated. The required public API is int zms_get_num_cycles(struct zms_fs *fs, uint32_t *cycles) and int zms_get_sector_num_cycles(struct zms_fs *fs, uint32_t sector, uint32_t *cycles), declared in the public ZMS header; on success they return 0 and store the requested 32-bit count in *cycles. A caller must be able to query the maximum recycle count across all sectors and the recycle count of any individual sector. These queries must reject a NULL file-system pointer or NULL output pointer (-EINVAL), must reject an out-of-range sector index (-EINVAL), and must reject an unmounted file system (-EACCES). For zms_get_sector_num_cycles, the sector argument is a 0-based sector index less than fs->sector_count. The returned count must grow correctly as sectors are recycled (e.g. after N sector advances it increases by the number of full recycle cycles), and the count must be preserved across zms_clear() and re-mounting rather than being reset to zero, even past the historical 8-bit counter wraparound at 256.
